chapter: Bass, drums and the big-band rhythm section
title: Double-jointed fingers and high strings on the bass
summary: Ramey explains why he sometimes fingers a note with two fingers and why his short notes came from strings set high.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

: Well, back to what I was saying ...Now this isn't copping a plea, but I've had guys to ask me why didn't I learn to play the bass properly, you know, 'cause they see me sometime with two fingers on one note. But I was born double-jointed.

: And I have no pressure in the balls of my fingers. In other words, you see it's that. You can't see it on the radio, I mean on the speaker there, but that is that. So, when I go to press a note, my finger does that. There's no--you see?
: Getting on there and staying on it...so I have to play like this.
: This probably accounts for when they talk of your long notes. It partly comes from that, doesn't it?
: Mostly, I mean, partly. You know, what was my trouble with the long notes was the fact that

I never gave up the big band style until about three years ago. So my strings--were usually just about in--In fact, guys still ask me, do I still have my strings a half inch off finger board. See, that's what makes me have the other short notes. It's louder, but your notes are very short because you got your strings so high off the finger board.
Yes, I see. I didn't know that, but I see it.
